# Current SDK divergences

This is the current retained surface, not an implementation log. Audited on
2026-09-12 (Pacific), including the verified replay, React cleanup and method
identity fixes, reconciled with Agents 0.26 on 2026-10-02, with Agents 0.27
on 2026-10-09 and with Agents 0.32 on 2026-10-31. The upstream baseline is
[Agents 0.32 / Think 0.23](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/be1749221ab3efc8be4e976d8e7d8344d1446032);
[VENDOR.md](../VENDOR.md) owns package provenance.

Update the owning row when behavior changes; remove it when the divergence is
retired. Each row needs a real consumer, reason it cannot be a host shim, proof,
and retirement condition. Git preserves the
[previous chronological record](https://github.com/WebMCP-org/do-runtime/blob/ff87e9ef1d38f8beaa579b3a53d445e62df96837/vendor/agents/docs/fork-diff.md).
The [current audit](audit/vendor-fork-audit.md) owns measured costs, upstream
issue findings and unresolved coverage questions. Test names below describe
inspected coverage; fresh follow-up results are identified explicitly in the audit.

## Local maintenance policy

Upgrades are forward-only. The fork preserves the migrations and regression
coverage needed to read existing actor data and queued work on upgrade.
Downgrading code against upgraded storage is unsupported; historical downgrade
limitations below explain this boundary and are not a rollback implementation
backlog.

The workspace manifests and Agents package snapshot exclude Evalite,
`packages/agents/evals/`, and the `evals` command. The sole retained evaluation
required model credentials and was outside the deterministic SDK gate. Removing
its unused runner avoids maintaining a separate development-server dependency
graph. Keep this exclusion during upstream syncs; runtime scheduling and its
deterministic tests remain maintained. The
[October audit](audit/agents-sync-2026-10-02.md#optional-evaluation-runner-exclusion)
records the decision and scope.

## 2026-09-14 — Preserve completion across a cold restart

- `packages/think/src/think.ts`: both chat streaming paths persist the assistant
  before broadcasting completion. `_streamCutoverOptions` keeps every chat turn's
  terminal stream record through the cutover until the next stream start
  reclaims it; upstream keeps it only for agent-tool children. A recovery task
  can outlive the message transaction; deleting its stream in that transaction
  made a cold wake continue an already-completed answer. This supersedes the 0.23
  refresh's immediate-discard behavior and its resume-specific discard policy.
- Think 0.19's submission outcome stamps (`result_status`, `output_json`) do not
  replace this. They cover only a running submission, so a plain WebSocket turn
  still needs the stream record. The stamps commit inside the retained cutover
  or `_finalizeSubmissionStream`, before completion is broadcast.
- Wire order follows upstream 0.26: persist, canonical transcript, then completion.
  The observer terminal merge retains canonical metadata while a replay ledger
  skips already-applied chunks. Fork continuation-prefix restoration applies only
  before the ledger has applied the replay, preserving cold-remount recovery.
  Resume offers retain their request owner: an unrelated terminal or stale ACK
  cannot release another offer. Think also holds ACK-driven completion until
  its transcript is published, including the interval after the producer closes.
  `terminal-frame-order.test.ts` holds the real assistant cutover and verifies
  that reconnect replay ends with `replayComplete`, then canonical history, then
  `done`; the regression failed before wiring the shared terminal-hold hook.
- No new storage shape, migration, timer, or recovery protocol. The existing
  `discard: false` cutover and start-time reclaim bound retention to the previous
  turn, as already used for agent-tool tailing and reconnect replay.
- Reproduced while validating [Rook #166](https://github.com/WebMCP-org/rook/pull/166):
  upgrading the published 1.1.0.509 profile, completing a second turn, and cold
  restarting could issue a third model request and duplicate the answer.
- `packages/think/src/tests/think-session.test.ts` observes durable assistant rows
  at terminal broadcast on both paths and recovers a real completed turn whose
  enclosing run survived cutover. Each regression failed before the fix.
  `stream-cleanup.test.ts` checks that the next turn reclaims terminal evidence.
  The upstream `submissions.test.ts` case "keeps only the completed stream, not
  the outcome stamp, after a submission settles" is adapted to that retention.
- Why no host shim: completion and stream-to-message transactions are private
  Think internals, shared by browser and Worker consumers. Upstreamable: yes.
  Retire when upstream keeps chat-turn stream evidence until the recovery Task
  settles.

## Ownership map

Rook's `ThreadApp` keeps the conversation socket and Agent-tool subscription
above transcript replacement. The shared React hook/AI SDK own the displayed
transcript; `WebSocketChatTransport` owns request delivery and resume. Think
owns admission, inference, transcript persistence and Stop. Agent owns parent
run records and child lifecycle. The runtime supplies Durable Object gates,
storage and browser context. Rook supplies Chrome resources and configuration.

Four state owners have different jobs: the socket buffer bridges absent hook
subscribers; the outbox retains requests with uncertain delivery; the Agent-tool
roster projects retained work; cancellation records whether children may still
execute. None is a second transcript store. Fix each ordering at its owner,
not with a host deduper, retry cache or recovery controller.

Paths below are relative to [`packages/`](../packages); shortened chat filenames
refer to `agents/src/chat/`. SDK behavior fixes are
upstreamable unless identified as product policy. Optional browser leaves are
upstreamable additions, not claims that Workers need browser polyfills.

| Cancellation and recovery: Agent `index.ts`, `agent-tool-types.ts`, chat `turn-queue.ts`, `recovery.ts`, `recovery-engine.ts`, `recovery-incident.ts`, and Think fence admission, retain uncertain child liveness, reconcile the SQL winner and drain accepted work. Think's `stopCurrentWork` is the fork's Stop-all (upstream has only the per-request `cancel`); it records a durable Stop epoch. Recovery callbacks check the Stop epoch and the per-request cancel in `_dispatchChatRecovery` before 0.29's `runRecoveryAttempt` admits them, so a stopped or cancelled turn is never sealed or reported to `onExhausted`, and is not counted against `maxInterruptedAttempts` unless the Stop lands while admission's `syncStorage` is in flight. The checks inside the callbacks remain. `recovery-engine.ts` adds two opt-in adapter fields; Think sets both and `AIChatAgent` sets neither, so ai-chat's admission and transition paths are upstream's (the owner-scoped recovering clear below applies to both packages). With `isRecoveryAttemptCancelled` (Think: the Stop epoch), an at-budget admission re-checks cancellation after its `syncStorage` (the incident's `user_cancelled` marker or the hook) and runs the callback instead of sealing; without the hook the engine seals at the budget, as upstream does, even when the incident was cancelled during the sync. With `sealedIncidentsAreFinal`, every engine writer that changes an incident's status honours the seal (`#finishAttempt` and `recordTransientRetry` write only counters onto the record and keep its status): `updateIncident` is a no-op on an `exhausted` record (no write, event or recovering-flag change); `beginIncident` never re-evaluates an `exhausted` record's budget, checking once after its first read and again on a fresh read immediately before its put, with no await in between, so a seal that lands while `readProgress` or `shouldKeepRecovering` runs is kept rather than overwritten with `attempting`; `scheduleRecovery` returns without the transition, the `chat:recovery:scheduled` event or the enqueue; and `rescheduleAfterStableTimeout` declines. Because a budget evaluation writes `exhausted` before its caller delivers the terminal UX, the record carries a `terminalDelivered` stamp, written only for opted-in hosts once the delivery has returned: by `markTerminalDelivered` after the fiber replay's and Think's stall path's `exhaustChatRecovery`, and in the same put as `exhaustRecoveryGiveUp`'s seal, which already follows its delivery. `beginIncident` returns a stamped record `sealed` (a replayed fiber or a later stall writes nothing, emits nothing and does not terminalize again; the replay keeps the settled partial and clears the recovering flag, leaving the stream row as the exhausted path does), and hands an unstamped one back as `exhausted` but not `sealed`, without a write, an event or a re-evaluation, so the caller delivers it and stamps it; a transient terminal-write failure or memory-limit reset between the seal and the delivery is therefore re-delivered on the retry, as upstream re-delivers it. Think's stall path skips the second banner only when the sealer's request id is its own; a continuation under the same root that stalls after a concurrent seal is terminalized under its own request id, so its clients get a done frame and a terminal record (a second `onExhausted` for the chain, the same at-least-once edge as a give-up re-run). A sealed incident therefore stays sealed: no Stop check, cancel, `failed` or `scheduled` write, budget re-evaluation, stable-timeout retry or racing completion can reopen it, including a callback that ran past a seal a duplicate delivery wrote during the same sync, and the engine's entry guard no-ops its later callbacks. Upstream's `updateIncident` overwrites any status. On a platform-transient callback error, `_handleRecoveryCallbackError` leaves the incident `scheduled` with the error as `reason` where upstream marks it `failed`: no `chat:recovery:failed` event is emitted, the recovering flag is set for the incident's root instead of cleared, and the incident stays active, so `listRecoverableChatRequests` still lists it and a per-request cancel can mark it `user_cancelled` while the platform retry is pending (the method's comment cites a 2026-07-31 ledger entry that no longer exists; this row now owns it). In both packages, `_recordTerminalChatStatus` clears the recovering flag only for the turn's own recovery root (the explicit root, else the admitted turn's root, else the request id), through `setChatRecovering`'s owner check in `recovery-incident.ts`; upstream (#1620) clears it whatever request owns it. Only `stopCurrentWork`'s unscoped clear removes any owner. A queued connection-less continuation carries that epoch in its payload, and child cancellation also dequeues it. The merged recovery body hands off through 0.19's `_runRecoveredTurnAfterAcceptance`. An auto-continuation's idempotent `finish` returns once Stop has cleared its pending and active slots; otherwise it delegates to 0.27's `_settleContinuationTurn` ([#2495](https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/pull/2495)). | Native Agent-tool lifecycle tests; Think reattach/recovery tests, including a second socket's queued request under Stop and under per-request cancel; durable-pause tests, including a queued continuation after Stop or child cancel; client-tool tests; Rook browser Stop/tab-cleanup tests; `think/src/tests/recovery-stop-seal.test.ts` (Stop and cancel near the budget, sealed-stays-sealed after Stop, no later transition reopens an exhausted incident, the exhausted list filter); the `recovery-engine.test.ts` cases for a cancel that lands while an at-budget admission syncs (with the hook, without it as upstream, and a seal kept when the callback's own Stop check runs after a concurrent seal) and the `updateIncident`, `beginIncident`, `scheduleRecovery`, `rescheduleAfterStableTimeout`, `exhaustRecoveryGiveUp` and fiber-replay cases for an exhausted record with and without `sealedIncidentsAreFinal` (a delivered seal left alone, an undelivered one handed back and stamped, a seal that lands during `shouldKeepRecovering` kept, `markTerminalDelivered` a no-op without the flag, a replay whose terminal delivery threw re-terminalized exactly once with and without the flag, and the sealed replay leaving the stream row alone); the platform-transient `testRecoveryCallbackError` cases in `think-session.test.ts`, which assert `scheduled` where upstream asserts `failed`; `recovery-incident.test.ts` "setChatRecovering ownership". | An abort signal does not prove child shutdown. Parent recovery precedes queue stability; later startup can repair an interrupted child after failed inspection. Stop preserves partial history and accepted sibling writes; a request admitted before Stop stays in history unanswered. Stated limitations, both upstream behavior: a request admitted while another turn runs is persisted before that turn's answer, so its model call ends with Think's continue checkpoint; a per-request cancel that arrives before admission persists the message is dropped, and that request runs. Fork residuals: a child cancel that lands after the root has already dispatched a queued connection-less continuation can still start that one turn on the cancelled child; a stale callback delivered after Stop for an incident that is already `skipped` writes `skipped`/`cancelled` again and re-emits `chat:recovery:skipped` (harmless); a Think turn that completes after a concurrent seal leaves the `exhausted` record for the TTL sweep instead of deleting it; `scheduleRecovery` returns nothing to say it declined, so a Think stall whose incident is sealed after its `beginIncident` still reports `scheduled` to its stream consumer (a `recovering` done frame after the sealer's banner); an `exhausted` record written by an older build, or by an evaluation whose delivery died, has no stamp and is delivered once more on its next opening; and no Think test reaches the stall path's request-id fall-through, which needs a seal that lands under a running continuation. A recovering flag that a terminal turn does not own stays until its owner's terminal, Stop, or the flag TTL. The 0.23 port uses upstream Tasks and retains these admission and cancellation contracts. The admission ordering retires when upstream checks cancellation before admitting a recovery attempt; the Stop-epoch hook retires with the fork's Stop-all; `sealedIncidentsAreFinal` retires when upstream makes `exhausted` terminal in `updateIncident`; the `scheduled` transient write retires when upstream stops marking a platform-retried incident `failed`; the scoped recovering clear retires when upstream scopes the terminal clear to the turn's recovery root. |

| Early model preparation and media: Think `prepareModel` and inference configuration select capabilities. `think/src/workspace-read.ts` wraps `@cloudflare/computer`'s `read` (`withWorkspaceReadMedia`, `createWorkspaceReadTool`, re-exported from `@cloudflare/think`): `workspaceAcceptsImages`/`workspaceAcceptsPdfs` gate image and PDF parts per render, before any file I/O, and the note quotes the size saved in the result. `workspacePdfText` renders a PDF as page text for a model without PDF input, cached by SHA-256 per extractor in an LRU of 64 entries (8 before the refresh). A result that carries bytes is gated whatever its size. A result without bytes is Computer's oversize result or a Think 0.20 one, which share a shape: over the smaller of the wrapper's and Computer's `maxModelBytes` (Computer's is found by rendering placeholder bytes, with no I/O) it stays an error even if the file later shrinks, and the model recovers by calling `read` again; under it, it is re-read as a Think 0.20 result with a current-size check before loading, and renders as a tool error, without changing history, when inaccessible. The re-read calls `workspace.fs` directly, so a `root` given to `createAITools` (and its symlink check) does not confine it; Think passes no `root`, and routing the re-read through Computer's `execute` would close this for hosts that do. Re-reading only helps hosts whose files survived the upgrade, such as Rook's host workspace; a Shell Workspace's files are not moved to a Computer Workspace. A declared image or PDF type is checked against the file's bytes before it is sent or extracted, on the PDF-model and text-extraction paths alike: image signatures are matched at byte 0 and a mismatched image is relabelled, a PDF needs `%PDF-` within its first 1 KiB (a BOM, newline or junk before it passes, as in PDF readers, Computer and Think 0.20), and anything else renders a note. A non-PDF file result passes to Computer's render unchanged. The media type comes from Computer's extension and bounded content sniffing instead of `stat.mimeType`: SVG reads as text, and HEIC/TIFF come back as Computer's `{kind: "binary", unsupported: true}` JSON instead of a "convert to PNG" note. Notes and errors give sizes in bytes instead of `formatSize` units, so each re-rendered 0.20 transcript changes text once. Computer's `read` carries the size preflight and bounded sniffing; the re-read drains with `getReader()` as Computer does. | Rook model configuration; `workspace-read-media.test.ts` (gates, PDF text, size preflight, Think 0.20 re-read, byte-type check, a tool set whose `maxModelBytes` differs from the wrapper's in either direction, the PDF header window on both paths) and `workspace-tools.test.ts` agent wiring. ## Browser filesystem and schema primitives

| Retained behavior and owner                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Consumer and proof                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Why it remains / retirement condition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shell/src/browser/directory-handle-workspace.ts` supplies a Workspace filesystem directly over an existing directory handle, using the shared native metadata and path leaves. `@cloudflare/shell/paths` and `/browser/native-file-system` expose those existing implementations without an actor or Workers bootstrap.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Rook's mounted folders keep handle persistence, permissions, namespace and MIME policy; Shell owns traversal, write rollback, lock coordination, copy/move and globbing. `browser-tests/directory-handle.test.ts` exercises real native handles: direct reads, shared locks with lossless append, aborted stream writes, binary-ordered pages, tree copy/move and missing-parent errors.                                                                                                                                                                                        | OPFS's private `data/` and `meta/` layout cannot represent an ordinary selected folder. This backend implements the SDK's filesystem contract and is reusable by browser hosts. Retire with equivalent public upstream directory-handle and pure path/metadata APIs.      |
| `shell/src/workspace-file-system.ts` is the existing filesystem adapter, separated from the state-backend factory and exported by the browser entry. It follows intermediate symlinks, consumes all directory pages (stopping when a backend that ignores `offset` repeats a page), and uses optional native `appendFileBytes` instead of racing read/concatenate/write.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Rook's live Bash adapter delegates these algorithms. The three real native browser regressions failed before the fixes: unresolved link path, 1000/1001 entries, and nineteen lost concurrent append bytes. `workspace.test.ts` lists 1001 entries through a proxy that ignores paging, the shape of upstream's own cross-DO proxy example.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Adapter behavior belongs to Shell's filesystem contract, and a browser-safe class must not eagerly import Node archive/hash utilities through an unrelated factory. Retire with equivalent upstream traversal, pagination, native append capability and pure class entry. |
| `codemode/src/json-schema-types.ts` owns raw type expressions through the framework-free `/json-schema-types` entry point; declarations and framework adapters use the same printer. Arrays print as `Array<T>` and intersection operands are parenthesized, so unions keep their precedence; an object without `additionalProperties: false` carries an index signature that also admits its named and optional fields; malformed/cyclic branches become `unknown`. TanStack `createCodeTool` returns its inferred tool type, keeping the code schema and literal name, instead of `ServerTool`. Upstream 0.5.6's `tool-types.ts` declaration helper `jsonSchemaToTypeDecl` is kept as an alias of `jsonSchemaToType`, so declarations still use this printer; it types an empty strict object as `Record<string, never>` where upstream prints `{}`. | Rook MCP signatures and OpenAPI declarations replace their parallel printer. `src/node-tests/json-schema-expression.test.ts` checks output with the real TypeScript compiler and bounds mutually inlined `$defs` (2.7 MB unbounded) and nested index signatures (185 MB); `tanstack-tool-types.test.ts` pins the TanStack type. Upstream's `tool-types.test.ts` expectations are edited for the printer's `Array<T>` (`:90-95`) and index signatures (`:206`, `:213`) without comments; only the `Record<string, never>` edit (`:256-257`) carries a vendor-divergence comment. | Schema projection is Codemode behavior shared across tool providers. One print stops at 100,000 emitted characters and prints later nodes as `unknown`, so a hostile schema cannot grow exponentially. Retire when upstream exposes the same API and these semantics.     |

## Deliberate product omissions

The skill script runner is omitted. `agents/src/skills/index.ts` exports no
`SkillScript*`/`SkillRunContext` types, and `skills/tools/ai-sdk.ts`'s
`createSkillTools(catalog)` takes no options (upstream 0.32's `SkillToolsOptions`
with its `scriptRunner` is not exported), so `run_skill_script` never exists. `agents/package.json` and `scripts/build.ts` carry no `./skills/runner`
entry. Think omits `getSkillScriptRunner()`, the `skills.runner` re-export
(`think/src/skills.ts`) and its top-level `SkillRunContext` type (`think.ts`).
`skills/{runner,script,script-workspace}.ts` stay upstream-identical but
unreachable, and upstream's `skill-runner.test.ts` is left out on syncs. They
stay byte-identical to upstream so the omission adds no sync diff beyond the
entry points.
Upstream's runner executes scripts in a Dynamic Worker through Codemode, which
needs a Worker Loader the browser host does not have. Fork tests pin the
absence: `agents/src/tests/skills.test.ts`,
`think/src/tests/skills-runner-omission.test.ts`,
`think/src/tests-d/skills-namespace.test-d.ts` and
`think/src/browser-tests/skills.test.ts`. Restore only with a browser Worker
Loader. Upstream docs that describe `run_skill_script` carry a one-line fork
note.

Think omits the Codemode runtime/approval composition. Think keeps upstream's
type-only `codemode?` field: 0.32's `ExecuteToolAgent` has no other member, so
without it `createExecuteTool(this)` stops type-checking; nothing in Think reads
it. Rook has one checked-code
executor. This is product scope, not an upstreamable runtime bug fix. Upstream's
`execute-hitl.test.ts` and its test agent cover that composition, so they are
removed with it; upstream syncs leave them out.
Think's `tools/execute.ts` is baseline-identical, and `codemode/src` carries no
execution, connector or approval patch: its only divergence is the schema printer
row above (`json-schema-types.ts`, `tool-types.ts`, `tanstack-ai.ts` and their
tests). Restore the composition only when the product intends to support it,
with its runtime and tests.

## Already upstream or retired

Do not reintroduce historical PartyServer transport, a duplicated native bridge,
`__unsafe_reconcileAlarm`, local SDK aliases/declaration augmentations, a custom
MCP runtime validator, old Codemode approvals/cancellation/log caps, the private
fetch-predicate export, `prepareRun`, or a Voice readiness shim. The baseline
already includes replay batching, default chat throttle, resume/finalizer fixes,
and native facet routing. History records their removal; the live inventory
must not keep them as work to maintain.

## Ownership and upgrade seams

Sessions, Streams, Tasks, DynamicAgents and the lifecycle job queue replace
the old experimental-memory provider, stream SQL implementation, recovery
continuation scheduler and progress KV counter. 0.24 moves Agent's state row,
queue and connection flags into the `State`, `Queue` and `WebSockets`
capabilities. These implementations are upstream-owned. Neither refresh
changes the browser runtime.

- `agents/src/sessions/compaction-helpers.ts` restores `protectHead` and
  `minTailMessages` options because Rook persists a whole tool loop in one row.
  `compaction-utils.test.ts` drives custom floors through real compaction;
  retire when upstream exposes equivalent policy.
- `agents/src/sessions/core.ts` restores `SessionMessage.createdAt` from JSON
  or its SQL creation time; an invalid lifted timestamp remains undated.
  `sessions/migration.test.ts` checks the one-way lift and undated fallback.
- `agents/src/chat/react.tsx` memoizes the existing approval response command.
  `default-throttle.test.tsx` verifies one identity across streamed messages;
  retire when upstream returns the same stable command.

The four SDK SQL lifts drop their source tables; selecting a 0.22 package pin
does not reconstruct them.
[The migration guide](rook-0.23-migration.md) records each historical lift. Completed-request receipts now survive until the
next stream starts, rather than a timed completed-buffer window.

0.24's first wake is also one-way. `cf_agents_queues` rows become Lifecycle jobs
and the table is dropped; Agent's `cf_schema_version` row moves to KV
`cf_agents:schema_version`; `State` and `Queue` record their own KV schema
versions. A 0.23 build on that database recreates an empty queue table, but its
job driver drops due `queue` jobs. This is another historical reason the fork
supports forward upgrades only. Upstream marks the queue-table lift as temporary (removed in the
next minor, so a deployment must pass through 0.24) and it drops legacy rows whose
payload is not valid JSON. `Agent.queue()` returns before its callback runs; the
callback runs from the next alarm.

Think 0.19 runs its submission drain, workflow notifications, connection-less
continuations and media-eviction passes as Lifecycle queue items, so each waits
for an alarm and runs one at a time. Its first start copies undelivered
`cf_think_workflow_notifications` rows into queue items and drops that table.
`cf_think_submissions` gains nullable `result_status` and `output_json` columns,
which a 0.18 build ignores. A 0.18 rollback recreates the empty outbox and
re-drives pending submissions from `cf_think_submissions`, but loses queued
continuation, media-eviction and workflow-notification items.

The provisional protected `Agent.webSockets` getter was removed before release:
Rook's 17 real browser delegation/Stop checks proved delegated facets have zero
physical sockets. Inherited virtual-connection broadcast already covers them;
the host override is deleted as well.

## Compaction chat synchronization

Think's Sessions change listener broadcasts its refreshed history through the
existing chat-message frame after `compact` and direct `compaction` writes.
Upstream Think 0.18 and 0.19 (`c076e4c9`) only refresh the server cache. The native
socket regressions reproduce stale connected history without these two calls,
including automatic compaction and virtual facets. Native React tests verify
that canonical overlays replace old history during sending and observing
streams without dropping reasoning, tool results, or subsequent text.

The former session status/error bridge is removed. Sessions' handle and Agent's
lifecycle sink again follow upstream; the design system consumes chat updates
and its existing manual command result. Retire the two broadcasts when upstream
Think synchronizes these writes itself. Configurable head/tail floors remain
independently justified by the small-row-count compaction regression above.

## October release integration

The 104 commits from the prior pin through Agents 0.26 were reviewed alongside
the package endpoint diff. Upstream now owns method override snapshots (#2165),
React result cleanup's pre-dispatch guard (#2403) and deleted-facet
lookup/socket lifetime (#2024). The fork's parallel implementations are removed.
The requested-address identity reset (#2394) is not taken:
`agents/src/react.tsx` deletes upstream's effect-time reset and derives
`identified` and `ready` during render from the delivering socket and
destination ("Socket-bound identity"). Upstream retry and continue recovery
callbacks replace the fork's unified helper; Stop epoch checks remain on both.

Think 0.20 requires AI SDK 7 and React SDK 4. Agents adds optional Pi/provider
peers; the new Pi integration is not a runtime dependency for other consumers.
Sessions adds a nullable content hash; Think adds submission message identity and
child event-delivery fields. Existing tables migrate in place. The previous
0.24 lifecycle-queue migration remains required under the forward-only policy.

TanStack AI 0.54 infers the browser tool's JSON-schema input as unknown. The
adapter, now in `agents/src/browser/tools/tanstack-ai.ts`, retains
its browser input contract and explicit literal tool name through
`toolDefinition<typeof core.inputSchema, undefined, TName>`; the heterogeneous
tool type regression (`tests-d/browser-tool.test-d.ts`) uses TanStack's current
`AnyServerTool`. Upstream pins TanStack 0.38; retire both adjustments when it
adopts 0.54. The 0.32 `web/search` and `web/fetch` adapters need neither: their
upstream type tests typecheck against 0.54 unchanged, and upstream now wraps the
search failure test's `execute` in `Promise.resolve` itself.

Agents 0.27 ([sync audit](audit/agents-sync-2026-10-09.md)) moves the first
Channels pass to `agents/experimental/channels*` and adds experimental
harnesses, the `agents` CLI, and Web Search tools. These are imported with the
release and are opt-in; no fork divergence was added for them. The daemon
bundle `src/harness/container/daemon-source.generated.ts` is generated at build
time, gitignored, and excluded from format and lint, as upstream does.

## Native recovery inspection

`Think.listRecoverableChatRequests()` exposes the framework's current request
and stable recovery-root identities before post-startup Task alarms run. It
inspects the canonical chat Task step journal, stash snapshots, pending recovery
callbacks and owed response hooks. Completed model steps, canceled Tasks, Stop
epochs, terminal streams without an owed hook, superseded callback targets
and recovery callbacks whose incident was sealed as exhausted do not create
live work. A successor replaces its predecessor within the same
root. The existing startup response-hook replay uses the same unfinished-step
inspection, so stale Task cleanup cannot suppress an owed terminal hook.

`ActiveTurn.recoveryRootRequestId` exposes the existing admitted-turn identity;
pending response hooks retain it across eviction. Hosts can retain one latest
input projection without treating a retry as a new input or reading private
Task SQL. Native Workers regressions exercise live model work, journal cutovers,
pending hooks, cancellation and successor correlation. Retire these additions
when upstream exposes equivalent semantic recovery inspection and stable roots.
